title: What training does BSEE's SEMS rule require for offshore oil and gas operators and contractors?
description: BSEE SEMS training under 30 CFR 250.1915: initial and periodic training, drills, change notices, contractor checks and audit cycles, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: Under 30 CFR 250 Subpart S, the Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement requires every Outer Continental Shelf operator to run a Safety and Environmental Management Systems (SEMS) program whose training element, section 250.1915, covers initial training, periodic training verified through drills, training or notice before personnel work under changed procedures, and verification that contractors are trained. Instructors' qualifications must be documented, and the whole program is audited by an accredited third party every 3 years.
keyTakeaways: Training is one of 17 mandatory SEMS elements listed in 30 CFR 250.1902, and section 250.1901(b) says all personnel involved with the program must be trained to perform their assigned duties.
Section 250.1915 requires initial training, periodic training using drills to verify retention, training or notice before personnel operate after a change, and verification of contractor training.
Stop Work Authority training must be part of orientation for all new personnel on the OCS, under section 250.1930(e).
An accredited audit service provider must audit the SEMS program within 2 years of initial implementation and every 3 years after that, and SEMS records are kept for 6 years.
A June 10, 2026 BSEE rule, effective August 10, 2026, updated incorporation-by-reference wording in Subpart S; API RP 75 Third Edition (2004, reaffirmed 2008) remains the referenced edition.
regulator: Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE), US Department of the Interior
appliesTo: Lessees and operators conducting oil, gas and sulfur operations on the Outer Continental Shelf
All personnel aboard covered facilities, which Subpart S defines as the operator's direct employees and contracted workers
Contractors performing work for the operator, other than domestic service providers such as catering and housekeeping
Mobile offshore drilling units when attached to the seabed, and DOI-regulated pipelines

sections.heading: What is the SEMS rule and how does training fit into it?

blocks.text: SEMS is BSEE's management system requirement for offshore oil and gas. Under [30 CFR 250.1900](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-30/section-250.1900), every operator must develop, implement and maintain a SEMS program that addresses the elements in section 250.1902 and the American Petroleum Institute's Recommended Practice 75 (API RP 75), which is incorporated by reference. Where Subpart S and API RP 75 conflict, Subpart S prevails.

Training is element 7 of 17. Section 250.1901(b) states the principle plainly: "All personnel involved with your SEMS program must be trained to have the skills and knowledge to perform their assigned duties." Section 250.1903 defines personnel as direct employees of the operator and contracted workers, so a training program that only covers the operator's own staff does not meet the rule.

Management carries the duty too. Under section 250.1909, management must ensure that suitably trained and qualified personnel carry out all aspects of the program, use personnel with expertise in developing training programs, and review the SEMS program at least annually.

Section [250.1915](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-30/section-250.1915) requires the SEMS program to establish and implement a training program so all personnel are trained in accordance with their duties to work safely and are aware of potential environmental impacts. Training must address operating procedures, safe work practices, emergency response and control, Stop Work Authority, Ultimate Work Authority, the Employee Participation Plan, reporting unsafe working conditions, and how to recognize hazards and construct and implement job safety analyses. The operator must document its instructors' qualifications.
The program must then address four specific components:

items: **Initial training** for the basic well-being of personnel and protection of the environment, ensuring people assigned to operate and maintain the facility have the knowledge and skills for their duties, including startup and shutdown.
**Periodic training** to maintain understanding of, and adherence to, current operating procedures, using periodic drills to verify adequate retention of knowledge and skills.

**Communication of change:** personnel must be informed and trained whenever a change to the SEMS program affects their ability to understand and perform their duties, and training or notice must be given before they are expected to operate the facility.
**Contractor verification:** how the operator will verify that contractors are trained in the work practices needed to perform their jobs safely and in an environmentally sound manner.

blocks.text: The rule does not set a refresher interval. The operator defines "periodic" in its own program, and auditors and BSEE then test whether that interval is set, justified and followed. The guide on [setting mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) covers how to justify one.

sections.heading: Which other Subpart S sections create training duties?

items: **Stop Work Authority (250.1930).** Training on SWA procedures must be part of orientation for all new personnel who perform activities on the OCS, and SWA procedures must be reviewed during all safety meetings. SWA must also appear as a standard statement in every job safety analysis.

**Emergency response and control (250.1918).** Emergency plans must be validated by drills on a schedule defined by the SEMS training program, with training and drills conducted periodically for all personnel, including contractors' personnel. Drills must use realistic scenarios, and each drill must be analyzed and critiqued to identify and correct weaknesses.

**Contractors (250.1914).** The operator must document that contracted employees are knowledgeable and experienced in the work practices for their jobs, verify that contractor personnel understand and can perform their assigned duties for activities such as maintenance, construction, turnarounds and specialty work, and evaluate contractor performance periodically.
**Reporting unsafe working conditions (250.1933).** Procedures for all personnel to report unsafe working conditions must be in place, with a visible notice posted at the place of employment.

blocks.text: Together these make SEMS training closer to a [competency-based](/glossary/competency-based-training) model than a course catalog: the rule asks the operator to verify retention through drills, verify contractors, and act on drill critiques.

sections.heading: How are SEMS training records audited and retained?

blocks.text: Through a third-party audit cycle and BSEE evaluations. Under [30 CFR 250.1920](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-30/section-250.1920), an accredited audit service provider must audit the SEMS program within 2 years after initial implementation and every 3 years after that, covering all program elements. The operator must submit the audit plan to BSEE at least 30 days before the audit, the audit report within 60 days of completion, and a corrective action plan within 60 days naming the person responsible for each fix.

Under [30 CFR 250.1928](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-30/section-250.1928), SEMS records and documents must be kept for 6 years, with SEMS program documents held at an onshore location. Shorter rules apply to some items: SWA training and reviews must be documented, kept onsite for 30 days and retained for 2 years, and job safety analyses and management of change records are retained for 2 years.

BSEE can also visit facilities under section 250.1924 to verify that personnel are following the SEMS program and that the operator can produce evidence of implementation. If it finds the program noncompliant, section 250.1927 allows Incidents of Noncompliance, civil penalties, or probation or disqualification as an OCS operator.

BSEE's final rule [Oil and Gas and Sulfur Operations in the Outer Continental Shelf: Documents Incorporated by Reference](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/10/2026-11648/oil-and-gas-and-sulfur-operations-in-the-outer-continental-shelf-documents-incorporated-by-reference), published June 10, 2026 at 91 FR 35304 and effective August 10, 2026, updated a large set of incorporated industry standards and changed the way Subpart S cites API RP 75. The listing still identifies API RP 75 as the Third Edition, May 2004, reaffirmed May 2008, and section 250.1915 was not amended.

Well control and production safety training sits in a separate part of 30 CFR 250, Subpart O, and is covered in [BSEE well control and production safety training](/regulations/bsee-well-control-and-production-safety-training). Operators should treat the two as complementary: Subpart O for specific technical duties, Subpart S for the management system around all personnel.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links each SEMS element to the training that supports it, records which drills verify which knowledge, and ties management of change records to the people who must be trained or notified before operating. That gives an audit service provider a direct line from section 250.1915 to individual evidence. More on how this applies across the sector is on the [energy and resources](/industries/energy-resources) page.

faqs.q: Does SEMS specify how often offshore personnel must be retrained?
faqs.a: No. Section 250.1915(b) requires periodic training using drills to verify retention, but the operator sets the interval in its SEMS program. BSEE and the third-party auditor then check that the interval is defined and followed.

faqs.q: Do SEMS training requirements apply to contractors?
faqs.a: Yes. Subpart S defines personnel to include contracted workers, section 250.1915(d) requires the operator to verify contractor training, and section 250.1914 requires documentation that contracted employees are knowledgeable and experienced in their work practices. Domestic service contractors such as catering are excluded from the contractor selection rules.

faqs.q: How long must SEMS training records be kept?
faqs.a: SEMS records and audits are generally kept for 6 years under section 250.1928. Stop Work Authority training records are kept onsite for 30 days and retained for 2 years, and must be available to BSEE on request.

An audit service provider accredited by a BSEE-approved accreditation body. The audit team lead must be from the provider and unaffiliated with the operator. Audits take place within 2 years of initial implementation and every 3 years after that, and BSEE may direct additional audits.
